notes:
I couldn't do this research. My search and page-reading tools stopped working on every try: the first attempt was cut off by a usage limit, and the next three (one page fetch and two searches) all timed out. I didn't read a single page, so I have no notes on Psalm 31 that come from the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any commentary from memory. That would mean unsourced claims and made-up URLs.

**Pages I would have read first:**
- Enduring Word: enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-31/
- Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub: biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/31.htm (and the same address with /gill/ or /pulpit/ in place of /ellicott/)
- NET Bible translator notes, for the modern scholarly view: netbible.org/bible/Psalms+31
- Augustine on the Psalms at New Advent, for the Catholic reading. Older Bibles number this Psalm 30, so check that numbering.
- Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (Spurgeon.org or CCEL) for the Baptist view, and Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu) for the Methodist view.
- Verse 5 ("Into Your hands I commit my spirit"), which Jesus says from the cross in Luke 23:46. This is the verse most likely to show differences between traditions and in Catholic and Orthodox readings, so I'd search sites like gotquestions.org, ligonier.org and oca.org for it.

If you want to try again, ask me in a new message and I'll write the notes verse by verse once the tools work. Or paste text from any of these pages here and I'll turn it into sourced notes in your format.
